title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS DEVELOP NOVEL SOCIAL BIASES THROUGH ADAPTIVE EXPLORATION

bias_targets.methodology: Simulated multi-turn sequential decision-making tasks (e.g., a hiring game, refugee resettlement, and military conscript assignment) where LLMs allocate jobs or resources to artificial or unfamiliar demographic groups with identical underlying success rates. Bias is measured using the Stratification Index (SI), Between-Group Divergence (BGD), and Group Assignment Stochasticity Index (GASI) to quantify how models develop novel stereotypes based on initial noisy feedback.

Replicating the multi-turn hiring game using real demographic labels ('White', 'Black', 'Hispanic', 'Asian') and stereotypically associated job categories to evaluate if models reproduce entrenched racial associations versus generating new ones, measured via Stratification Index and GASI (Appendix I).
